articles.title: Coach Crispin Chettri not let down by loss
articles.summary: KOLKATA: For those following Indian women’s football, it might have felt like four blows as Russia hammered in four goals en route a dominant win on a
articles.body: KOLKATA: For those following Indian women’s football, it might have felt like four blows as Russia hammered in four goals en route a dominant win on a rainy evening on Thursday.But for coach Crispin Chettri it was just a learning curve that his young team, with an average age of 23, were on in their bid for a spot in AFC Women’s Asian Cup in 2029.“I would rather lose now than not qualify for the Asian Cup,” Chettri said at the post-match interaction at Kishore Bharati Krirangan. “I take all the blame that we played a certain way tactically.”Chettri did not have the likes of Manisha Kalyan or Soumya Guguloth – with the former playing mid-season in Greek top tier for AEK Athens to guide the Indian attack and the latter one of the Indian stars not released by East Bengal in the middle of preparations for AFC Champions League games – or a Sweety Devi to man the defence.But the coach, who acknowledged that “every coach wants his best players to play”, still believes that the match was an opportune stage for the youngsters to perform under pressure in his bid to increase squad depth ahead of the continental qualifiers.“But see Manisha and other are already playing in the best team. When they are not there, few young players get a chance to play with this kind of a competitive team. So, that was my idea,” explained the coach, who has been brought back at the helm after choosing to go with foreign coach for the last Asian Cup in Australia.I’m not complaining that somebody didn’t release the players. That's part and parcel of the game. But it was also a blessing. Two three young players did show their character. So now those who didn’t play are in trouble. If the youngsters start performing, then the competition grows and I have options in selecting the players. That’s how I would move forward.”The 51-year-old also pointed to the areas where improvement was necessary to compete at such high levels as with the world No. 27 Russians after the Indians wilted physically after giving a fight in the opening 40 minutes.“I think we have seen a few things where we lack today. But I think the main problem was our fitness. But we can’t improve our fitness in two days,” he said, having trained with the team in the city from Sept 18.“So, if we could carry the character that we showed in the 40-45 minutes to 60 minutes. That’s a step forward. I would start working with the youngsters towards that end and then take it forward.”With the 69th-ranked team set to take on Russia in a second friendly on Sunday, Chettri can gauge if his young squad has made any progress in challenging their superior opponents.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Cedae Saúde: Ex-dirigentes sob suspeita compram clube em Portugal | G1
articles.standfirst: Sócios do Amora Futebol Clube desde 2025, Eric Gualberto e Antônio Carlos dos Santos aparecem em mais um capítulo das investigações sobre a Cedae Saúde, que já apontaram pagamentos de R$ 95 milhões a empresas ligadas a uma offshore e o custeio de despesas médicas de Cláudio Castro.
articles.summary: A auditoria na Cedae Saúde ligou Eric Gualberto e Antônio Carlos dos Santos a desvios de R$ 95 milhões e ao custeio de despesas médicas de Cláudio Castro.
articles.body:
A auditoria que apontou indícios de desvios superiores a R$ 400 milhões na Cedae Saúde identificou uma ligação empresarial entre o ex-presidente da entidade, Eric Gualberto , e o ex-diretor financeiro da Cedae, Antônio Carlos dos Santos .

Segundo os documentos analisados, eles se tornaram donos do Amora Futebol Clube , equipe da 2ª divisão do Campeonato Português, em agosto de 2025.

O governo do RJ fez uma auditoria sobre a gestão da Cedae Saúde entre 2023 e 2026 . O balanço apontou que 4 empresas ligadas a uma offshore atribuída a Eric Gualberto , nas Ilhas Virgens Britânicas, receberam R$ 95 milhões durante o período em que ele esteve à frente da entidade.

Em outra frente da apuração, documentos obtidos pela TV Globo mostraram que o então governador Cláudio Castro foi incluído como beneficiário da Cedae Saúde , embora nunca tenha sido funcionário da companhia. Segundo a atual gestão da entidade, ele acumulou uma dívida de R$ 140 mil com o plano de assistência médica.

De acordo com o levantamento, a antiga gestão da Cedae transferia à Cedae Saúde valores muito superiores aos necessários para o custeio da operação.

Parte desses recursos foi destinada às empresas de tecnologia ZIL Projetos Ltda. e T7, que receberam juntas R$ 48 milhões entre junho de 2023 e junho de 2026.

Os auditores registraram que o volume de recursos destinados à área de tecnologia chamou atenção porque a sala de TI da Cedae Saúde possui apenas um computador e tem como único funcionário um jovem aprendiz. A atual administração informou que suspendeu os pagamentos às empresas.

O relatório da auditoria será encaminhado aos órgãos responsáveis pela investigação.

A defesa de Eric Frederik Gualberto repudiou as acusações e disse que foi o principal prejudicado, tendo sido afastado da Presidência da Cedae Saúde sem poder se defender.

Os advogados também questionaram a legalidade e a imparcialidade da auditoria e afirmaram que vão tomar as medidas judiciais cabíveis.

Em nota, Cláudio Castro afirmou que nunca solicitou adesão ao plano de saúde da Cedae Saúde. Segundo ele, foi informado pela própria diretoria da entidade de que tinha direito ao benefício e recebeu a carteirinha para utilização dos serviços.

Sobre a dívida, o ex-governador disse que nunca recebeu boletos ou cobranças mensais e que só tomou conhecimento do débito há cerca de uma semana. Castro afirmou ainda que fará o pagamento dos R$ 140 mil cobrados pela entidade.

articles.title: Lutador de jiu-jitsu abre academia e transforma vidas em Araçatuba | G1
articles.standfirst: Marco Aurélio ocupa a 13ª posição no ranking mundial da modalidade. Hoje, ele ensina o esporte para cerca de 70 alunos na própria academia em Araçatuba (SP).
articles.summary: Marco Aurélio ocupa a 13ª posição no ranking mundial da modalidade e hoje ensina o esporte para cerca de 70 alunos na própria academia.
articles.body:
A árdua rotina de vender garrafas d'água e doces nos semáforos em Araçatuba , no interior de São Paulo, foi deixada para trás após um lutador de jiu-jitsu, de 21 anos, realizar seu maior sonho: abrir a própria academia.

Os esforços de Marco Aurélio Lovato de Oliveira deram resultado positivo há cerca de seis anos, quando ele deixou o trabalho autônomo e apostou no esporte. Hoje, a história do faixa preta que acumula títulos internacionais e uma trajetória marcada pela superação, sendo consagrado campeão mundial, virou inspiração para outros jovens.

Campeão mundial de jiu-jitsu já vendeu água no semáforo para arrecadar fundos para competir internacionalmente — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Marco também ocupa a 13ª posição no ranking da Federação Internacional de Jiu-Jitsu Brasileiro (IBJJF) na categoria meio-pesado. Além do título mundial conquistado em 2021, ele coleciona medalhas no Campeonato Brasileiro, no Sul-Americano e em etapas do Open internacional, tendo competido em países da Europa, nos Estados Unidos e nos Emirados Árabes Unidos (Dubai).

Marco Aurélio já conquistou título mundial de jiu-jitsu em 2021 — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

A participação em grandes competições levou o lutador a viajar e a conhecer outros países.

"Hoje estou entre os melhores do mundo, lutei com os melhores, ganhei de muitos. Consegui fazer várias viagens através daquele passo que dei. Para mim, o que dá mais orgulho, fora as medalhas, foi o ranqueamento que tive", destacou o atleta em entrevista à TV TEM.

Campeão mundial de jiu-jitsu abre academia em Araçatuba (SP) e dá aulas para crianças e adultos — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Depois de tantas conquistas e títulos ao longo da carreira, Marco Aurélio passou a focar em um novo desafio: formar atletas de jiu-jitsu. A experiência adquirida durante os anos em que praticou a arte marcial o inspirou a ministrar aulas para jovens e adultos.

Com muito esforço, trabalho e reconhecimento, o jovem conseguiu montar sua própria academia em janeiro deste ano. No começo, não havia alunos e o espaço correspondia à metade do tatame que possui atualmente. Pouco a pouco, a estrutura foi crescendo e já são cerca de 70 alunos matriculados.

Cauã Ribeiro dos Reis está entre os alunos. O garoto começou a aprender jiu-jitsu com o professor e descobriu que o esporte pode lhe ensinar muito mais do que técnicas de luta.

"Jiu-jitsu é uma maneira de, como muitos acreditam, você aprender um esporte e além disso, uma proteção, desenvolvendo várias habilidades", contou Reis.

Para manter vivo seu sonho, o faixa preta de jiu-jitsu também contou com a parceira fundamental da esposa Ingrid Teixeira. Ela ajuda na efetivação das matrículas e cuida da parte administrativa da academia enquanto Marco se dedica aos treinos e aos alunos.

De perto, Ingrid acompanha cada conquista e se orgulha ao ver o marido transformar as dificuldades do passado em oportunidades para ele e para outras pessoas.

É gratificante, né? Porque foi uma caminhada bem longa e a gente vê que ele veio do semáforo, não ficou lá apenas por querer um dinheiro extra . Ele foi, continuou no semáforo, dia, noite, frio ou não e fez aquilo se tornar uma realidade, conquistar o seu sonho de ir para fora, de lutar, competir e não só isso, de abrir a própria academia, disse a esposa.

Esposa de atleta de Araçatuba (SP) campeão mundial de jiu-jitsu ajuda-o a administrar própria academia — Foto: Reprodução/TV TEM

Hoje, Marco enxerga nos alunos um pouco daquele menino que um dia também sonhou em chegar ao topo. Talvez por isso, mais do que ensinar uma técnica, ele quer que a nova geração acredite nos próprios sonhos e não desista.

" Amo essa oportunidade de dar aulas todos os dias para criança, adulto e poder ver realmente, hoje, o que é viver do jiu-jitsu. Eu percebo que a geração de hoje, às vezes, não acredita nos próprios sonhos. Viver do meu sonho é algo que não tem preço", ressaltou Marco.

articles.title: Russia find a way to keep football alive despite FIFA and UEFA ban
articles.summary: KOLKATA: “Personally, it’s very hard on any footballer,” Russia defender Veronika Kuropatkina said in broken English after asking her team interpreter to
articles.body: KOLKATA: “Personally, it’s very hard on any footballer,” Russia defender Veronika Kuropatkina said in broken English after asking her team interpreter to let her answer STOI's questions on her own.The Zenit St Petersburg player, happy to be in India for the first time, is here for the two international women's friendlies, the second of which will be played at Kishore Bharati Krirangan here on Sunday.It’s one of the rare international appearances for the Russians in an unofficial international friendly, with the country banned by FIFA and UEFA since Feb 2022, a fallout of Russia’s war on Ukraine.“The situation, it’s hard on every one of us. And it’s not just about football, it’s about life,” said the centre back and a backbone of the Russian defence.They, however, have regular leagues and championships to keep plying their trade and getting match practice, a vital reason for their superiority in the first match on Thursday against the Indians, who last played a competitive game in June.And Russia head coach Yuri Krasnozhan was glad that he still gets the chance to scout for and keep strengthening his squad, despite the lack of international competition.“You know, football exists in countries not only with the aim of participating in some international competitions. But there’s the aim to develop it in the country,” Krasnozhan explained to STOI in an exclusive chat.“And women’s football in Russia has been developing so fast in the last eight or 10 years despite everything. I can’t compare it with any other sport in the country but the improvement in football is very high,” he continued.“Of course, we feel the lack of official international games. But, on the other hand, we can try new talents and bring some young players to the national team. Playing international games would surely increase the players’ experience. But now we have the opportunity to develop our young talents.”The visitors, here with a younger squad, showed that quality on the pitch in their 4-0 win despite having had just one training session in India and playing in conditions vastly different from those in Russia.India coach Crispin Chettri also used the opportunity to give the younger Indian players exposure to international football and had as many as six debutants in the game and his goal on Sunday is to see his team extend the quality it showed in the opening 40 minutes and convert the chances that come their way.For the Russians, however, it’s another international sojourn that won’t be counted in FIFA records, no matter how well the world No. 27 perform on the field.“We have the championship, and we play together and we play between ourselves. articles.title: Vinicius apologises for hair-pull red card but could miss El Clasico
articles.summary: Real Madrid forward has a goal disallowed, is sent off for the hair-pull offence and could miss the next three games.
articles.body:
Real Madrid’s Vinicius Jr has apologised ⁠⁠to ⁠⁠his teammates and the club’s fans after being sent off in the 1-0 ⁠⁠win over Villarreal in La Liga at the Santiago Bernabeu but now faces a ⁠⁠nervous wait for a ruling by the disciplinary committee, which could see him miss Real’s fixture with rivals Barcelona in two weeks.

The Brazilian thought he had scored Real’s second goal in the match on Saturday, but his effort was disallowed after a video assistant referee (VAR) review found he should be dismissed for pulling Nathan Saliba’s hair in the build-up.

After the match, Vinicius, ⁠⁠who came on in the ⁠⁠52nd minute and was red-carded 20 minutes later, posted on social media, saying, “sorry to the team and the ⁠⁠fans”.

Vinicius was celebrating after scoring when referee Isidro Diaz de Mera was called by the VAR to review the moments before his goal. The referee waved off the goal and pulled out a red card for Vinicius.

When he thought Vinicius had doubled the lead, Real manager Jose Mourinho ran to join the celebrations with his players.

But moments later, Vinicius was left livid by the referee’s decision. He screamed at Diaz de Mera while his teammates tried to calm him down as he left the field.

“I don’t think he meant to hurt anyone, but it is a red card,” Villarreal defender Juan Foyth said about the hair yank of Saliba.

Diaz de Mera wrote in his match report that after being shown the red card, Vinicius “protested my decision, raising his voice, toward where I was standing in an aggressive manner, and being held back by teammates”.

Royal Spanish Football Federation regulations state that pulling an opponent’s hair ⁠⁠is regarded as violent conduct.

The ⁠⁠sanction for violent conduct without causing injury to an opponent, according to Article 130 of the league’s rules, is a ban of one to three ‌‌matches.

Real’s next three La Liga games are against Sevilla, Barca and Racing Santander, but missing El ‌‌Clasico ‌‌would be a bitter blow for the 26-year-old Brazil international.

Mourinho did not appear at the mandatory post-game news conference.

articles.title: What can Man City expect against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday?
articles.summary: Man City face Liverpool in their first game since being found guilty of serious EPL financial breaches.
articles.body:
Red flares, smoke-filled pyrotechnics, strongly worded banners and trenchant chants.

Manchester City can expect a raucous and hostile reception when they arrive at Anfield for their Premier League match against Liverpool on Sunday.

Liverpool supporters are angry, and they are planning to parade their emotions for City as the league leaders play their first match since being found guilty of breaking more than 100 financial rules .

In a decision that could have a drastic effect on the future of the English top flight, an independent commission found that City and their Emirati owners had arranged “sham” deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.2bn) from 2009 to 2018.

City, who deny any wrongdoing, have appealed against the devastating verdict.

The multiple breaches of Premier League regulations came during a period when City won three league titles and a clutch of other trophies while Liverpool struggled to break City’s stranglehold on the game in England.

City were given a taste of the resentment that awaits them when Manchester United fans goaded them during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Man City’s players and manager Enzo Maresca will get the full taste of a potentially fiery reception from Liverpool fans, who have also waited three weeks to watch their team back in action after the extended international break.

Social media posts and video reactions have made no secret of the anger that will be directed towards City by Liverpool’s supporters.

Spion Kop 1906, a Liverpool supporters group that organises flag and banner displays on The Kop, the famous single-tier south stand at Anfield, urged attendees to come prepared to show their support when the Reds host Man City.

“There’s loads riding on Sunday’s game on and off the pitch, but it’s down to us as a collective to bring the noise and get behind the team,” Spion Kop said on X.

“Bring your flags, bring your scarves and be at it from the very first minute.”

A social media post promoting a “Bus greeting”, urging Liverpool supporters to gather near ‌‌‌‌the stadium several hours before kickoff ahead of the arrival of the City players’ bus, is also making the rounds on X.

Another post about the bus greeting took a dig at Man City, describing the match as “LFC vs Cheats”.

Merseyside Police said there would be an appropriate policing operation ⁠⁠⁠⁠in place on the day of the match.

Liverpool fans are no strangers to creating a hostile welcome for City.

In 2018 during a Champions League quarterfinal tie, City’s team bus was attacked with bottles and flares when it arrived at Anfield. Liverpool were subsequently fined 20,000 euros ($22,400) by UEFA, European football’s governing body.

Dom Farrell, author of the book Glory Days for the Waifs and Strays, which chronicled City’s rise from the third tier to European champions, expected Sunday’s showdown to be “massively hostile”.

“If they were to win against Liverpool and then beat an off-form Paris Saint-Germain [in the Champions League on Wednesday], you really get a siege mentality going,” Farrell told the AFP news agency.

“But there’s also a decent chance they get turned over, and then it just starts to feel like you’re in this sort of dead zone waiting for the verdict.”

Former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville expected Sunday to be a “brutal day” for visiting Man City, who lead the standings with a 100 percent record and are six points ahead of Liverpool.

“If they want an understanding of how angry the game is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe,” Neville said on The Overlap podcast.

“I suspect there may be banners. There will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield.”

articles.title: "No puede ser que lo de Vini sea roja y lo de Fede no"
articles.standfirst: El vestuario del Madrid, muy molesto también con el trato "despectivo" de una parte del equipo arbitral ante el Villarreal
articles.summary: El vestuario del Madrid, muy molesto también con el trato "despectivo" de una parte del equipo arbitral ante el Villarreal
articles.body: Apenas unas horas después del complicadísimo triunfo ante el Villarreal, las aguas siguen revueltas en el Real Madrid en lo que al tema arbitral se refiere. Los jugadores del club blanco no escondieron su incredulidad en el mismo vestuario del Bernabéu. La roja a Vinicius centró sólo una parte de las quejas. Aunque se admite que la sanción pudo ser adecuada, la plantilla se mostraba incrédula ante la inacción del VAR en acciones que pudieron beneficiar al Madrid en otros partidos, como el pasado derbi. “Lo que no puede ser es que un tirón de pelo sea roja y la entrada del otro día a Fede pase de largo”, se pudo oír en la caseta de los blancos tras el triunfo del sábado ante el Submarino. La expulsión de Vini no fue el único detalle que disgustó a los madridistas, que vieron cinco amarillas y una roja tras cometer tan sólo ocho faltas, por las dos cartulinas tras 13 infracciones de sus rivales. Quizá lo que más enfadó a los blancos fue el trato "despectivo" de los asistentes de Díaz de Mera y del cuarto árbitro, con el que José Mourinho se encaró en varios momentos del partido. El entrenador del Madrid acabó muy caliente el partido, razón por la cual decidió no ofrecer rueda de prensa tras el choque. "No hablo porque quiero estar en el banquilo ante Sevilla y Barcelona", comentó Mou a sus más cercanos. Vini era, obviamente, el jugador más afectado tras todo lo ocurrido en el partido. Suplente de inicio, su salida al campo revolucionó el ataque del Madrid, hasta que se produjo la acción que acaparó titulares tras el duelo. El brasileño comentó a sus compañeros que la acción con Saliba fue un enganchón involuntario y sin intención alguna de hacer daño al rival, que de hecho siguió en la jugada que acabó en el gol anulado al delantero brasileño. En la caseta dieron por buena la versión del 7. "Él es incapaz de hacer eso", comentan. En cualquier caso, y ante la redacción del acta por parte de Díaz de Mera, en el Madrid dan por hecho que Vini se perderá el Clásicodel próximo 25 de octubre, ya que la sanción, incluso contando con un recurso exitoso por parte del club, será como mínimo de dos partidos. Por otra parte, el club recurrirá la amarilla mostrada a Konaté en los últimos minutos del partido por una presunta falta a Gerard Moreno. Las imágenes demuestran que el defensa del Madrid no toca al atacante del Villarreal, y en el club están convencidos de que la amarilla será retirada. De mantenerse, será la cuarta amonestación para el central en tan sólo 8 partidos de Liga. La pasada temporada, en la Premier, vio sólo siete tarjetas amarillas en 36 partidos.

articles.body: Después del triunfo del sábado en Mendizorroza que acabó de espantar los fantasmas sobre el rendimiento lejos del Metropolitano (ya son nueve puntos de 12 posible en las cuatro salidas del campeonato) y de consolidarse como el primero de los perseguidores del Barcelona en el liderato de LaLiga, el Atlético ya tiene su mirada en la visita del Manchester United de este próximo martes en la Champions. Así que, sin tiempo que perder, Simeone ya dirigiría en la mañana de este domingo la primera de las dos sesiones previas al duelo, si bien estuvo condicionada por el partido frente al Alavés. De ahí que los que fueron titulares, acompañados de Julián Alvarez, Baena y Sorloth, se sometieron a una sesión regenerativa y de trabajo personalizado mientras el resto saltaban al verde. Así, serían los que no tuvieron minutos en Vitoria, como Pubill, Hjulmand o Arnau Ortiz, los que más exigencia tuvieron antes de unirse con el grueso de los disponibles, entre los que sobresalían Kang-in Lee y Hancko (disputaron apenas media hora frente al cuadro babazorro), en el trabajo con balón. Una sesión que El Cholo aprovecharía para incidir tácticamente con los mediocentros: tanto el danés como Obed Vargas, Mendoza y Castillo. Así las cosas, no será hasta el entrenamiento del lunes cuando El Cholo cuente con todos los efectivos a sus órdenes. Será por tanto la única oportunidad que dispondrá para trabajar el plan que ronda su cabeza para medirse al Manchester United.

Last week she scored the third goal as England beat Greece 3-1 in their 2027 World Cup play-off semi-final first leg.

articles.title: Elton John: Former Watford owner 'upset and disappointed' with Championship club's form
articles.summary: Former Watford owner Elton John says he is "upset and disappointed" by the club's form following their 4-0 home defeat by Burnley.
articles.body:
Former Watford owner Elton John has said he is "upset and disappointed" by the club's form following their 4-0 home loss to 22nd-placed Burnley.

The Hornets sit 20th in the Championship table having lost three straight league games and five of their past six.

In a now-deleted response to a club post on Instagram , external , the global music star said: "As a lifetime supporter of Watford FC, I am very upset and disappointed at the decline over the past few weeks.

"I really feel for the supporters who have to watch this."

Watford appointed Alessio Dionisi as their manager in June on a two-year contract, with the Italian becoming their 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season.

His side negotiated a challenging start to the season well, beating Southampton at Vicarage Road and then drawing away at Wrexham and at home to West Ham.

They have picked up points in just one of their subsequent fixtures, beating Preston 2-1 at home last month.

They were 3-0 down inside 25 minutes on Saturday, going on to lose to a Burnley side who had previously won one league match in 2026, against Crystal Palace in the Premier League in February, and had not won an away fixture in almost a year.

Childhood Watford fan John has had two spells as the owner of Watford, initially overseeing their rise from the fourth tier to a second-placed finish in Division One and European football under Graham Taylor in the 1970s and 1980s.

Returning to takeover the club in the mid-1990s, he re-appointed Taylor, who took the club into the Premier League in 1999 with successive promotions.

The 79-year-old, who released a book, Watford Forever, in 2024 that detailed his relationship with the club and has a stand named after him at Vicarage Road , relinquished control of his boyhood side for a second time in 2002.

Former Watford captain Troy Deeney also spoke of his fears for the club on X , external , saying "the writing is on the wall and has been for months".

Deeney, who scored 140 goals in 319 appearances for the club, listed "removing talent", "allowing for poor standards" and "a lack of accountability" among the issues with the club, stating in a follow-up post , external that he was "never bitter, some times angry at what I see".

The Hertfordshire side have not finished higher than 11th since relegation from the Premier League in 2022.

Speaking on an official club podcast this week, chairman Scott Duxbury said: "We've got a lot of players who people on the outside will say shouldn't be here. They're here because they believe in what we're trying to achieve but this has to be a season where we achieve it.

"I'm tired of seasons where we say on paper we've got a great team and we fade away. This year, no excuses, we've got to achieve our potential and have a successful season."

articles.title: Athenea, destrozada: "Ha sido sin querer…"
articles.standfirst: Patri Guijarro y Eva Navarro salieron en su defensa, mientras una periodista cuestionó su reacción en la retransmisión de Telemundo
articles.summary: Patri Guijarro y Eva Navarro salieron en su defensa, mientras una periodista cuestionó su reacción en la retransmisión de Telemundo
articles.body: Athenea del Castillo terminó entre lágrimas una noche que difícilmente olvidará. La internacional española terminó desconsolada en el vestuario después de ver la tarjeta roja directa ante Estados Unidos, en una acción que empañó el triunfo de La Roja en Washington. Sus compañeras cerraron filas en torno a ella, aunque la jugada también provocó comentarios críticos durante la retransmisión del encuentro. Athenea llevaba apenas unos minutos sobre el césped cuando, en una disputa por el balón, agarró del pelo a Michelle Cooper. La estadounidense cayó al suelo y la acción acabó revisada por el VAR. La colegiada mexicana Diana Pérez acudió al monitor y mostró la roja directa a la futbolista del Real Madrid, que dejó a España con diez en los últimos instantes del partido. Casualidades de la vida, la acción ocurrió cinco minutos antes de la expulsión de Vinicius por el mismo motivo. La futbolista del Madrid abandonó el campo entre los abucheos de parte de la grada. La imagen de la madridista, abatida tras lo ocurrido, contrastó con la victoria española por 0-2 y con la defensa de sus compañeras tras el partido. "Estamos con Athenea, estoy segura de que no fue intencionado, ni de mala fe. No es agradable, estaremos con ella", explicó Patri Guijarro. También Eva Navarro quiso arroparla: "Es normal que esté así, fastidiada. No he podido ver todavía la acción, pero entiendo que ha sido sin querer. Solo nos queda animarla". La expulsión no fue el único foco de debate. Durante la retransmisión del encuentro en Telemundo, la periodista Carlota Vizmanos hizo un comentario crítico sobre la reacción de la madridista y su historial de acciones similares que ha corrido como la pólvora en redes sociales. "Se ríe Athenea, dice que no, pero es una jugadora que a lo largo de toda su carrera ha estado bastante acostumbrada a este tipo de acciones, por no decir otra cosa", señaló.

articles.title: Billy Sharp retires after incredible 22-year career
articles.summary: Sheffield United legend Billy Sharp announces his retirement from football at the age of 40.
articles.body:
Sheffield United legend Billy Sharp has announced his retirement from football at the age of 40.

Sharp, who played for Southampton, Nottingham Forest, Leeds United, Hull City, Scunthorpe United, Reading, Doncaster Rovers and Rushden & Diamonds during a 22-year professional career, during which he scored 299 goals.

He had been a free agent since leaving Doncaster at the end of last season, when he signed off in style in his final game with a hat-trick against Peterborough.

"I'm going to hang my boots up. I've given it a good ride. I've got a long way, got to 40," Sharp told Sky Sports.

"I wanted to go out on my own terms. I've seen many friends get taken away by injury and things like that.

"I wanted to go out with a bang and luckily for me, I got a hat-trick in my last appearance.

"I'm maybe not the most talented player, maybe not the most liked on the pitch but that's because I love football. I'm passionate and I think I've got every single bit out of my career.

"I've made memories in football that will last me a lifetime."

A boyhood Blades supporter, Sharp made his Championship debut off the bench against Watford in November 2004.

He went on to become club captain and an important figure in three promotion-winning campaigns - from League One in 2017 and the Championship in 2019 and 2023.

In three spells with Sheffield United, Sharp scored 129 goals for the club and became a Blades icon.

He was also part of the Southampton side that won promotion to the Premier League in 2012.

He enjoyed a brief stay in the MLS with LA Galaxy in 2023, after which many thought retirement loomed - but the ageless Sharp returned to his native Yorkshire to extend his career, firstly with Hull and then Doncaster Rovers.

Sharp scored a dramatic late winner against Bradford City to secure promotion to League One for Rovers in 2025 before his spectacular ending to last season which meant he had scored EFL hat-tricks in his teens, 20s, 30s and 40s. He did score a fourth against Peterborough which would have taken him to 300 career goals but it was ruled out for offside.

"It would have been lovely to have got that 300th goal on that day but I've had an unbelievable career," he said.

Sharp has joined Baller League team N5, which is led by former Arsenal and Germany goalkeeper Jens Lehmann to play six-a-side football but he also has one eye on management having completed his coaching badges.

articles.summary: Carlos del Cerro y César Soto estarán en el VAR en el partido Inter-Brujas
articles.body: El sueco Glenn Nyberg, el italiano Marco Guida y el alemán Daniel Siebert han sido designados para dirigir este martes los partidos Atlético de Madrid-Manchester United, Galatasaray-Barcelona y Villarreal-Nápoles, respectivamente, de la segunda jornada de la Liga de Campeones. Nyberg estará auxiliado en las bandas por sus compatriotas Mahbod Beigi y Andreas Soderkvist y con Kristoffer Karlsson como cuarto árbitro, mientras que en el VAR estarán los neerlandeses Pol van Boekel y Dennis Higler. El colegiado nórdico, de 37 años, dirigió el pasado febrero el partido de ida de la ronda de clasificación para los octavos entre el Brujas y el cuadro del argentino Diego Pablo Simeone, que concluyó con empate a tres tantos. Guida dirigirá al Barcelona en Estambul ante el Galatasaray, con Giorgio Peretti y Giuseppe Perrotti como asistentes, Fabio Maresca cuarto árbitro y Marco di Bello y Aleandro di Paolo en el VAR. El italiano, de 45 años, también se reencontrará con el equipo de Hansi Flick, al que pitó en la ida de los octavos de final el pasado marzo en el campo del Newcastle (1-1), así como dirigió al Barcelona en la fase de grupos de la Liga de Campeones 2023-24 en el campo del Amberes, donde perdió por 3-2. En La Cerámica, Siebert pitará al Villarreal ante el Nápoles con Jan Seidel y Rafael Foltyn como jueces de línea, Max Burda como cuarto árbitro y Soren Storks y Bastian Dankert en la sala VOR. El conjunto castellonense está invicto con el germano. Bajo su arbitraje empató a tres en el campo del Spartak de Moscú en octubre de 2018 y ganó por 0-1 al Dinamo de Zagreb en abril de 2021, en ambos casos en la Liga Europa, mientras que en la 'Champions' firmó un empate en casa ante el Juventus en febrero de 2022. articles.title: Courtois regresa al lugar donde todo empezó
articles.standfirst: El portero belga vuelve a REAL, la marca de guantes que le acompañó en sus primeros pasos, tras adquirirla y estrenar esta nueva etapa con una portería a cero ante el Villarreal
articles.summary: El portero belga vuelve a REAL, la marca de guantes que le acompañó en sus primeros pasos, tras adquirirla y estrenar esta nueva etapa con una portería a cero ante el Villarreal
articles.body: Thibaut Courtois ha cerrado el círculo. El guardameta belga vuelve a REAL, la marca de guantes que le acompañó en sus primeros pasos hacia la élite, pero esta vez lo hace de una manera muy diferente. Después de tres años vinculado a Elite Sport, el portero del Real Madrid inicia una nueva aventura empresarial recuperando una parte de su historia. El cambio no responde únicamente a una cuestión de patrocinio. Courtois ha adquirido una marca belga de guantes de portero y ha decidido defender la portería madridista con sus propios productos. Así lo anunció Elite Sport en un comunicado en el que confirmó el final de una relación de tres años y deseó éxito al internacional belga en su nueva etapa. "Thibaut ha adquirido una marca local de guantes de portero belga y ha elegido usar guantes de su propia marca", explicó la compañía. La firma elegida es REAL, vinculada a los primeros pasos de Courtois en el fútbol de élite, cuando comenzó a despuntar con el Genk. Aquel joven portero que empezaba a llamar la atención por sus condiciones es hoy uno de los referentes mundiales bajo los palos. Ahora, el belga quiere trasladar su experiencia al otro lado y construir un proyecto propio dentro del mercado de los guantes de portero. Courtois estrenó sus guantes en el encuentro ante el Villarreal y terminó con la portería a cero en la victoria en el Bernabéu. El belga volvió a demostrar que su influencia sigue estando bajo los palos. Con el Madrid defendiendo una ventaja mínima y obligado a resistir en inferioridad numérica tras la expulsión de Vinícius, Courtois apareció en un momento clave para evitar el empate. Su intervención ante Carlos Romero en el minuto 77 fue decisiva para regalar los tres puntos a los de Mourinho. Un disparo desde dentro del área que Courtois leyó a la perfección para despejarla a córner de manera milagrosa. Cuatro intervenciones y una nueva portería imbatida completaron una actuación que dio al regreso de REAL el mejor escenario posible.

articles.title: Derry City: Silverware trumps Europe for Duffy
articles.summary: Derry City captain Michael Duffy says winning a trophy takes priority over qualification for Europe as he scores both goals in the Candystripes' FAI Cup semi-final win over Galway United.
articles.body:
European qualification was the furthest thing from Derry City captain Michael Duffy's mind before Saturday's 2-0 win over Galway United in the FAI Cup semi-final.

Behemians' 2-0 defeat by Waterford in Friday's first semi-final means there will not be an added European place available through the league, but this was an irrelevance for Mark Connolly's men.

Instead, reaching the cup final was all that mattered and should they defeat Waterford in the final on 8 November and reach Europe by this route, it will be a nice bonus but silverware is the primary objective.

It has been a turbulent campaign for City with interim boss Connolly stepping in after the dismissal of Tiernan Lynch in August, but they are now just 90 minutes away from the club's seventh cup win and first since 2022.

"You don't look at a cup like 'let's win the cup for Europe'," Duffy told BBC Sport NI.

"It's a cup, you want to win trophies and be successful here.

"It was all about getting to the final to win a cup, so it didn't add any pressure.

"We said that before, forget about Europe and that result last night as it means nothing - just go and get to the final and try to win the cup."

'We're encouraged to play free-flowing football'

Duffy scored both goals in Derry's win at Eamonn Deacy Park to send his side into the final and was understandably emotional at the final whistle, aware that " it was so importnat we got to the final this year".

"It's been a tough year all round," he continued.

"Now we can get a real buzz around the town this month, build it up and get that good feeling back between us all. We've a brilliant day to look for ward to."

Derry City's form has imporved since Connolly's appointment in August as they have removed any fears of relegation while reaching the cup final.

Duffy praised the impact of the former defender who he feels has liberated the team to express themselves on the pitch.

"He's letting us play free-flowing football, encouraging all the defenders to try and play football as we're all good players," Duffy said.

"He wants us to take risks and we're constantly doing that every day in training. Before matches he's saying that if we lose the ball, that's on him.

"He's enclouraging us so much and it's so enjoyable to play in. I think you can see that in these last few weeks were we are dominant and playing some nice football, but the main thing is players are digging in massively.

"You can see on the pitch it means everything to every player."

Derry City book place in FAI Cup final with Galway win

Duffy can now look forward to what he feels will be a "proud day" when he leads his home-town club out at the Aviva Stadium.

Waterford will provide the opposition following their victory over Bohemians and Duffy is expecting a tough task against Graham Coughlan's side.

"Our games against Waterford this year have all been tough," noted.

"They are a hard team to play against so it will be a hard game, but we look forward to it now.

"I can't wait for it, so hopefully walk out with my wee man [son] as well, so it will be a special day and something to look forward to.

"Hopefully I'll be bringing that cup back to Derry."

articles.title: Luís Castro: “No me ha gustado el parón, pero he podido recuperar a jugadores con molestias”
articles.standfirst: El técnico portugués del Levante ha confirmado que ni Etta Eyong ni Hugo Sotelo podrán estar disponibles
articles.summary: El técnico portugués del Levante ha confirmado que ni Etta Eyong ni Hugo Sotelo podrán estar disponibles
articles.body: A Luís Castro el parón internacional no le ha gustado. El técnico portugués ha calificado que no ha sido de su agrado la ventana de selecciones, ya que, “en términos competitivos, nos hubiera gustado que no hubiera sido tan larga”. Así mismo, ha confirmado que no ha podido recuperar a Etta Eyong ni Hugo Sotelo y que ambos no podrán estar disponibles para el choque ante el Sevilla. Lado positivo al parón: “A mí me gustaría que no hubiera sido tan grande, pero hemos trabajado en algunas cosas para mejorar. Nos dio tiempo para recuperar algunos jugadores que tenían molestias, pero pienso que, en términos competitivos, nos hubiera gustado que no hubiera sido tan largo”. Etta Eyong y Hugo Sotelo: “Hugo no está y Etta, tampoco. Este último empezó ayer la parte del calentamiento y un ejercicio que no tenía problemas en general. Hoy ha hecho el principio del entrenamiento. Está cerca de poder venir” Motivación en el parón: “Tenemos que preparar entrenamientos con calidad y entrenamientos para motivar a la gente. Hacer ejercicios que les gusten a los jugadores, para que estén más motivados. También hemos hecho ejercicios de detalles individuales para mejorar. Dentro del parón, tenemos que ver que cosas podemos aportar en el equipo”. Diego Moyano: “A mí me ha sorprendido de todo lo que han hablado de uno más que ha venido a entrenar. Más de veinte canteranos han venido a trabajar aquí. El filial jugaba viernes y yo no quería ningún jugador de ellos para que pudieran preparar el partido, al igual que el juvenil B y necesitábamos de un central y vinieron dos. Es un jugador que tiene proyección. Yo no miro los cadetes y no conocía muy bien, es una cuestión de la comunicación de dentro del club. Antes del entrenamiento ya había salido algo antes de la prensa. Yo no sé quién lo ha filtrado. Tiene catorce años y queda mucho para trabajar. No sé si volverá a entrenar más en el primer equipo, si necesitamos a un central, será uno del filial”. Seis partidos en 19 días: “Es lo que hay. No es lo mejor para los jugadores, tanto tiempo sin competir, pero es lo que hay. Vamos a intentar, dentro de la plantilla que tenemos, hacer lo mejor posible en todos los partidos” Internacionales: “Nosotros ya miramos a Axel antes de venir, no necesitaba mirarlo con Francia. Si juega o no, dependerá de su trabajo y el trabajo de su competencia. El resto de los internacionales ha sido bueno para ellos. Han tenido minutos y han podido jugar. En esas edades es bueno jugar para su evolución”. Sevilla: “Un Sevilla que aún no ha perdido fuera y está muy cómodo jugando fuera. Uno de los equipos más fuertes de la liga y son de los más agresivos. No toma riesgos y es eficaz. En este momento están en una posición buena por eso mismo y los equipos fuera de casa están bien. Será un partido duro” Adaptación de Ratkov y Musuayi: “Una de las buenas cosas del parón han sido ellos. Han trabajado muy bien y están cerca de lo que queremos. Pueden ser más útiles ahora de lo que eran antes. Pueden tener más minutos, aunque tenemos a Iván. Ellos están más cerca”

articles.title: El juicio por el 'caso Al-Thani' está más cerca de lo previsto
articles.standfirst: El TSJA quiere acelerar el proceso
articles.summary: El TSJA quiere acelerar el proceso
articles.body: La justicia ya tiene a Rakan Al-Thani entre rejas. El hijo del jeque se encuentra desde ayer en la prisión de Soto del Real, en el norte de Madrid, después de que la jueza instructora decretase su ingreso en prisión provisional, comunicada y sin fianza. Su llegada a España puede marcar un antes y un después en el 'Caso Al-Thani', una causa que se arrastra desde hace años y que ahora podría dar un paso decisivo hacia el juicio oral. El Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Andalucía (TSJA) contempla que, si Abdullah Al-Thani y sus hijos Nasser y Nayef no son localizados en un plazo breve, el procedimiento avance con los acusados que ya están a disposición de la justicia. En ese escenario, se abriría una pieza separada para los tres miembros de la familia Al-Thani que permanecen en paradero desconocido, permitiendo que la causa principal siga su curso. De esta forma, Rakan Al-Thani y los cinco exdirectivos españoles del Málaga CF, Moayad Shatat, Joaquín Jofre, Manuel Novo, Vicente Casado y Roberto Cano, serían los acusados que continuarían dentro del procedimiento encaminado al juicio oral. Algunos de estos antiguos responsables del club ya han reclamado que la causa se juzgue cuanto antes. La situación de Abdullah Al-Thani, Nasser y Nayef es diferente. Los tres continúan en paradero desconocido y sobre ellos pesa una orden europea de busca y captura. Si no son localizados próximamente, su situación quedaría fuera del procedimiento principal mediante esa pieza separada, evitando que su ausencia siga bloqueando el avance de la causa. La detención de Rakan Al-Thani en el aeropuerto de Múnich el pasado 12 de septiembre fue el primer gran movimiento en meses dentro del procedimiento. Tras ser trasladado a España, compareció por videoconferencia ante la jueza instructora y se declaró inocente, negando cualquier participación en los hechos que se le atribuyen. La magistrada decretó entonces su ingreso en prisión provisional, una medida solicitada por el Ministerio Fiscal y por la mayoría de las acusaciones, con la excepción de la representación de BlueBay. Además, la comparecencia permitió al juzgado notificar personalmente a Rakan las distintas resoluciones dictadas durante el procedimiento que hasta entonces no habían podido ser comunicadas a los miembros de la familia Al-Thani. Con Rakan ya a disposición judicial y Abdullah, Nasser y Nayef todavía en paradero desconocido, el 'Caso Al-Thani' afronta ahora un escenario que puede ser determinante para desbloquear definitivamente su llegada al juicio oral.

articles.summary: El canterano fue sancionado con tres partidos la temporada pasada tras tirar del pelo a un rival en la eliminatoria de ascenso del Madrileño frente a la Ponferradina
articles.body: Aunque la expulsión de Vinicius el pasado sábado por agarrar del pelo a Saliba provocó la indignación en el Real Madrid, existe un precedente no muy lejano. Curiosamente, en un Atlético que ahora 'aguarda' con expectación la sanción al brasileño después de que Iker Luque lo sufriera en sus carnes la temporada pasada. Cabe recordar que el canterano rojiblanco, ahora en el Racing, fue expulsado en la eliminatoria del playoff de ascenso a Segunda frente a la Ponferradina por el mismo motivo. Iker Luque, en este caso en un córner a favor del Madrileño, realizó un leve tirón al pelo de su adversario, siendo expulsado tras la consiguiente revisión. De nada le serviría al Atlético presentar un recurso al Comité de Apelación, pues sería desestimado e Iker Luque sería castigado con tres encuentros por "producirse de manera violenta al margen del juego, no estando en posibilidad de disputar el balón o el juego detenido, procediendo la sanción en su grado máximo atendiendo a las circunstancias". Así las cosas, todo lo que no sea una sanción igual supondría una sorpresa en el Metropolitano teniendo en cuenta cómo procedió el Comité en el caso de Iker Luque. De hecho, el canterano rojiblanco no reaccionaría del mismo modo que Vinicius una vez que vio la roja, con lo que se entiende que, al menos, el castigo no puede ser inferior.

articles.title: 'We preach emotional maturity:' Kalen DeBoer says he 'would have never expected' Dijon Lee's late personal foul in loss to Georgia
articles.summary: Lee's penalty gave Georgia a first down and allowed the Bulldogs to kneel out the clock in their 20-17 win.
articles.body:
Would Alabama have had a chance to tie Georgia or even get the win without Dijon Lee's late personal foul penalty?

The sophomore cornerback was called for a personal foul late in the No. 6 Crimson Tide's 20-17 loss to No. 2 Georgia on Saturday night. After Alabama stopped Georgia on second down to set up a third-and-2 just after the 2-minute warning, Lee's last smack of Georgia wide receiver Craig Dandridge at the end of the play gave the Bulldogs a free first down and allowed them to simply kneel out the clock.

When Lee came to the sidelines, Alabama coach Kalen DeBoer was furious. We'll let you lip read what DeBoer was saying to Lee. It might have been about costing Alabama a chance at a comeback.

After the game, the first question of DeBoer's news conference was about Lee's penalty.

"We preach emotional maturity and I really feel strong that across the board we had that with our team and would have never expected that to happen," DeBoer said. "You've got to give yourself a chance … You're out there giving everything you've got, you've just got to give yourself a chance. Emotional maturity is what it comes down to and we've been pretty good at that going on the last two years and obviously, moment comes up like we had just now, we didn't respond the right way."

Of course, there's no guarantee that Alabama would have gotten the ball back if Lee hadn't been penalized. Bo Walker gained seven yards on first down before his one-yard gain on second down to set up that short third down. With just two yards to go — and the benefit of the 2-minute warning to think about the call — Georgia had plenty of play options to go for the first down itself.

Instead, the Bulldogs didn't need to exercise any of them.

articles.title: Motherwell 0-2 Celtic: Hoops secure first win in four games to ease pressure on Martin O'Neill and go top in Scottish Premiership
articles.summary: Report as Celtic beat Motherwell 2-0 at Fir Park to go top of Scottish Premiership; goals from Camilo Duran and Benjamin Nygren made the difference; Martin O'Neill avoids fourth straight defeat and alleviates pressure on himself
articles.body:
After three losses before the international break, including two against Old Firm rivals Rangers, O'Neill declared his intention to not step down claiming that it would have been "poor" to do so .

Chris Sutton claimed pre-match that the 74-year-old should have walked away from the job during the break, but O'Neill's decision was rewarded by a pummelling performance from the Hoops.

Goals from Camilo Duran and Benjamin Nygren in either half were enough to claim the points, though the scoreline failed to show the true scale of Celtic's dominance.

Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen made a season-high 12 saves to prevent things from getting worse for the hosts.

His heroics were not enough to stop the inevitable result though, as the win sees Celtic go above Rangers at the top of the table and O'Neill avoids losing four straight games like the man he replaced in the dugout last season, Wilfried Nancy.

9: GOAL! Camilo Duran fires Celtic ahead with low drive from outside the box.

11: OFF THE LINE! Duran denied by Emmanuel Longelo who clears off the line.

52: DOUBLE SAVE! Paulsen saves from full-backs Colby Donovan and Kieran Tierney in quick succession.

57: OFF THE POST! Mika Baur's near-post flick beats Paulsen but comes back off the woodwork.

59: GOAL! Paulsen can do nothing to stop Nygren from doubling Celtic's lead.

61: CHANCE! Duran has a carbon-copy chance to Nygren, but Paulsen is on hand to stop him.

70: FINGERTIP SAVE! Another special save from Paulsen to deny Callum McGregor.

75: SUB! Jota makes his return to action after 18 months on the sidelines.

O'Neill: Celtic needed to get back to the basics

Celtic boss Martin O'Neill speaking with Sky Sports:

"We maybe just needed to get back to basics. The things that makes the club tick and the team go strong. All of those particular things I thought were in evidence.

"When you've lost a couple games and big matches, you have to look inwards and see what you can improve on. Of course, in some of the matches, there was a lot we could improve on.

"I think essentially it was back to what makes us strong. Pressing and the ability to play the ball when we had it."

Celtic defender Kieran Tierney speaking with Sky Sports:

"That was much more like us. I think we could've taken a couple more chances to be honest. We were working hard. It was evident to see the press was on and everybody was working together, tracking back. The tempo was just much better.

"It was a tough week. You know what it's like here. If you don't win there is scrutiny on you. That's not for us to get carried away, it's one win. We just need to build on it."

Johansson: We didn't profit from our moments

Motherwell boss Alfred Johansson speaking with Sky Sports:

"We were the second-best team. There were moments in the game where we managed to do our thing and do what we want to do and it works. But, there are also two easy goals we conceded which we need to improve on.

"After the first goal we built up some momentum, but you need to profit from those moments when you play a good team. We didn't.

"We come to the second half. We started okay but they were putting us down. When you concede the second goal and the way you concede it, it opens up the game. We are in a situation where we put ourselves there. They looked dangerous on some transitions. In the end, you will always be one step behind."

What the result means and next fixtures...

articles.title: Seedorf entrenará a Corinthians tras seis años alejado de los banquillos
articles.standfirst: El neerlandés se compromete con el 'Timao' hasta finales de 2027
articles.summary: El neerlandés se compromete con el 'Timao' hasta finales de 2027
articles.body: Clarence Seedorf (Paramaribo, 1976) está de vuelta. El exentrenador del Deportivo (2018) regresa a los banquillos tras seis años sin equipo, desde que saliera de Camerún en julio de 2019. El que fuera jugador del Real Madrid sustituye a Fernando Diniz al frente de Corinthians. El neerlandés, de 50 años, se compromete por lo que resta de temporada y otra más, hasta finales de 2027. "Aceptar este reto es un honor, pero también una gran responsabilidad. Estoy aquí para darlo todo y construir un equipo que luche por cada balón, cada minuto, cada victoria", asegura Seedorf, que, previamente, dirigió, también, a Milan (2014) y Shenzhen FC (2016). Sin embargo, habrá que esperar. Se espera que Seedorf, que cerró su carrera jugando en Botafogo (2012-14), aterrice en Brasil en los próximos días. Por tanto, no estará en el banquillo en el 'Clásico' ante Palmeiras. Es cierto que Seedorf, que tendrá a sus órdenes a Jesse Lingard y Memphis Depay, no era la única opción para entrenar al 'Timao'. También sonaron Ramón Díaz, Juan Pablo Vojvoda, Carille, Luis Zubeldía, Sylvinho y Mascherano.

articles.title: Hull City 2-2 Everton: Mohamed Belloumi earns Tigers point in thrilling four-goal second half with Toffees still unbeaten
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Hull City earn draw with Everton after four-goal second half; Everton remain unbeaten in Premier League; Joe Gelhardt opens scoring; Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall heads in equaliser; Thierno Barry puts Everton ahead; Mohamed Belloumi equalises off bench
articles.body:
Hull led shortly after half-time when Joe Gelhardt capitalised on a mistake from Everton right-back Ainsley Maitland-Niles, sending a delicate chip past Jordan Pickford in the 49th minute.

But Maitland-Niles soon atoned for his error with an inch-perfect cross for the outstanding Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, who nodded in the equaliser and the first goal Hull have conceded at the MKM Stadium this season, after a VAR check ruled out Brennan Johnson's opener for offside in the first half.

Everton created eight big chances and five fell to Thierno Barry, who finally took one, finishing past Konstantinos Tzolakis to put the visitors ahead after good work from Dewsbury-Hall to make the most of Sorba Thomas's loose pass.

However, Hull were not finished, and within six minutes they levelled when the dangerous Belloumi, benched after the international break due to tiredness, beat Pickford with a low shot shortly after coming on.

37: EVERTON GOAL RULED OUT! Johnson forces the ball in after Hull goalkeeper Tzolakis drops a cross, but VAR sends referee Michael Salisbury to the monitor and he rules it out for offside.

44: OFF THE LINE! James Tarkowski gets a crucial touch to turn Gelhardt's shot wide.

45+2: CHANCE! Barry heads over Jack Grealish's cross from close range.

49: GOAL! Gelhardt capitalises on Maitland-Niles' mistake to finish past Pickford.

55: EQUALISER! Dewsbury-Hall nods in the leveller from Maitland-Niles' cross.

60: BARRY MISSES A SITTER! The Everton striker has a tap-in from inside the six-yard box, but completely misses the ball.

68: BARRY GETS HIS GOAL! At last, Barry finds the net with a confident finish after being played through by Dewsbury-Hall.

74: GOAL! Super-sub Belloumi beats Pickford with a low strike from inside the area.

Everton manager David Moyes speaking to Sky Sports:

"A really frustrating day. We get a draw and it's a decent point away from home. Hull have done really well here but we should have won the game. We had very few performing today. I'm frustrated with it a little bit.

"There were not many performing at the level I think they have been or can perform at. I could hardly pick a player out who I could give a pass mark.

"When we went 2-1 up, I didn't think they could come back. We were so comfortable and didn't look like we should be conceding. A couple of defensive lapses were really poor.

"Everybody needs to step their game up."

Hull City head coach Sergej Jakirovic speaking to Sky Sports:

"Crazy second half. We started very well, they made one mistake and we punished it, but unfortunately we made two mistakes.

"I'm very happy with the boys because we showed a great mentality and we equalised. It's a good point for us.

"Everton are still unbeaten after six games. It's difficult to beat them. They have high tactical discipline and are strong in challenges, especially the centre-backs. It was not easy but we scored two nice goals."

articles.title: Crystal Palace 3-1 Nottingham Forest: Oliver Glasner's Selhurst Park return ends in defeat as Eagles complete remarkable comeback
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Crystal Palace come from behind to beat Oliver Glasner's Nottingham Forest 3-1 in their first reunion since his summer exit; Dan Ndoye gave Forest the lead before goals from Daichi Kamada, Jefferson Lerma and Yeremy Pino completed a turnaround
articles.body:
Glasner received warm applause before kick-off in recognition of the trophies he delivered at the club. But as Palace took control the mood changed, with chants of 'Glasner, what's the score?' and 'sacked in the morning!' ringing around the stadium.

Palace owed much to Walter Benitez, who produced a string of superb saves to deny Liam Delap, Morgan Gibbs-White and, later, Chris Wood. His interventions kept the hosts in the contest as Forest dominated early on, before Daichi Kamada's first Premier League goal and Jefferson Lerma's first-half stoppage-time header turned the game around.

Yeremy Pino extended Palace's lead in the 59th minute, reacting quickest after Matz Sels saved Jorgen Strand Larsen's effort. It ended a run of 19 Premier League appearances without a goal for the Spaniard and capped a remarkable shift in momentum, with Palace looking increasingly dangerous after the break.

The win ends Palace's 14-year wait for a league victory over Forest and gives Pierre Sage's side a much-needed boost after a difficult start to the campaign. For Glasner, a return that began with appreciation ended with taunts from his former supporters - a reminder that, in football, sentiment only lasts until kick-off.

Palace's victory lifts them to 12th in the Premier League table on seven points from six games, while Forest are 14th on five points.

3: GOAL! Forest take an early lead as Anan Khalaili's attempted header back to his goalkeeper falls straight into Ndoye's path, and the forward produces a superb finish.

7: SAVE! Kamada crosses for Strand Larsen, who forces Sels into a fine stop before the Forest goalkeeper denies him again.

21: SAVE! Benitez tips Ndoye's header over the bar as Forest continue to threaten.

28: CLOSE! Daniel Munoz meets Neco Williams' cross at the far post with a side-footed half-volley but sends his effort wide.

35: CROSSBAR! Gibbs-White rattles the woodwork before Benítez produces a stunning point-blank save to deny Delap from doubling Forest's lead.

41: GOAL! Palace are level as Kamada slots home after the ball breaks kindly into his path inside the area. His first Premier League goal survives a VAR check.

45+4: GOAL! Palace complete a remarkable turnaround before the break as Lerma heads home a superb delivery, with the ball slipping through Sels' legs.

59: GOAL! Palace extend their lead! Strand Larsen's effort is saved by Sels but Pino reacts quickest to slot home the rebound after a VAR check.

76: SAVE! Benítez produces another excellent stop to deny Wood from close range, keeping Palace's two-goal advantage intact.

90+5: FULL-TIME! Palace come from behind to beat Forest 3-1, ending their long wait for a league victory over the visitors and spoiling Glasner's return to Selhurst Park.

Analysis: Sage produces throwback Palace display in front of Glasner

Sky Sports' William Bitibiri at Selhurst Park:

"Crystal Palace have shown signs of rediscovering their attacking spark under Sage, with their 3-1 comeback win over Nottingham Forest the latest example.

"The Eagles have now scored three or more goals in two of their last four league games - as often as they managed across their previous 37 Premier League matches combined.

"Goals were a problem during Glasner's latter days in charge, as Palace struggled to balance their domestic and European commitments.

"There is an early sense of a throwback to the more free-scoring side that flourished under the Austrian in his first season, when their pace, movement and attacking combinations made them a threat to anyone.

"It is still early in Sage's tenure and two high-scoring performances do not guarantee a lasting change. But Palace look to be playing with greater freedom and confidence, with Kamada, Lerma and Pino all finding the net against Forest.

"If Sage can sustain that attacking momentum while tightening up a defence that has been vulnerable this season, there are encouraging signs of a more dangerous Palace taking shape."

Sage: It wasn't about revenge on Glasner

"It's not about revenge, a confirmation or something like this for every individual player. It's only about one game in a big series.

"The game is not against Oliver. The game is against Nottingham and that's the most important thing.

"We just have to be respectful with him, with what he did here. He helped me a lot because this team knows and is able to do a lot of things, and I have to thank him for that.

"It's not normal to concede too many chances as we conceded today. We had a problem in the first half, especially in the area of Ndoye. We have to be more efficient in one-vs-one situations when we defend.

"We have to be honest with what happened on the pitch. Everybody is aware of that, every player is aware of that, but I want to underline one thing: they give their life on the pitch."

Glasner: I was surprised but grateful for Selhurst reception

Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner :

"I want to say a huge thank you to the Crystal Palace supporters for this great reception. I didn't know what I could expect but it just shows the wonderful memories we created together here.

"I haven't experienced that I was supported from both sides and so a really huge thank you."

On whether he expected such a positive reception:

"I didn't expect but I thought it will be like this to be honest, because we had such great times together and this is just how I got to know them - very grateful fans, people."

"I think in total we played our best performance in the entire season. But again, if you don't score from all these chances... but there's nobody to blame because the effort was massive.

"Even after the 1-3, the players tried and tried and tried, and then effort created chances.

"I'm 100 per cent encouraged by this. Today I saw many positive performances, but it's not shown by the result because we missed the most important thing: scoring goals in the right moments."

articles.title: Otro triunfo de locos de la Real
articles.standfirst: El conjunto txuriurdin llegó a ir ganando por 3-0, pero se quedó con un futbolista menos a falta de media hora y vio como un meritorio Dépor casi le quita una victoria que le coloca sexto
articles.summary: El conjunto txuriurdin llegó a ir ganando por 3-0, pero se quedó con un futbolista menos a falta de media hora y vio como un meritorio Dépor casi le quita una victoria que le coloca sexto
articles.body: La Real Sociedad venció por 3-2 al Déportivo de A Coruña en Anoeta y se sitúo sexta en la clasificación, tras un partido en el que los txuriurdin estuvieron a punto de malgastar un 3-0, al marcar dos tantos los visitantes y rozar una igualada que quizás pudieron merecer. El Dépor notó enseguida la titularidad de Yeremay, cuya primera carrera cortó in extremis Sarr, con Remiro metiendo una mano tensa para desviar el remate cercano que hizo en la segunda aproximación al área rival, saliendo luego rápido el ex portero internacional a los pies de Nsongo, en la tercera llegada visitante. Después la Real se estiró, por fin, con un disparo de Barrenetxea que se estrelló en el lateral de la red de la meta defendida por Leo Román, que luego no se dejó sorprender por el intento de gol olímpico de Carlos Soler, con Zakarhyan no encontrando finalizador a su buena jugada, como sí la tuvo de inmediato el centro de calidad del valenciano en un saque de esquina botado en corto que Jon Martín cabeceó como él sabe de bien al fondo de la red. Los de Matarazzo le habían dado la vuelta, era evidente, al dominio inicial de los gallegos, a los que el tanto en contra les hizo daño, tanto que poco más tarde Zakharyan aprovechó un balón suelto en la frontal del área para sacarse un zurdazo con el que mandó la pelota lejos del alcance de Leo Román. Soriano pudo acortar diferencias antes del descanso, pero Sarr apareció para meter una pierna y evitarlo, con una buena mano de Remiro antes de pasar por los vestuarios. El Dépor volvió mejor al campo y merodeó bastante el área de la Real pero, tras reclamar un penalti a Luismi Cruz que ni el árbitro ni el VAR consideraron punible, Barrenetxea lanzó a la contra a Guedes, que realizó un espectacular control que aprovechó para con un potente disparo cruzado sentenciar el choque poniendo el 3-0. Matarazzo e Hidalgo realizaron cambios, pero fue Mario Soriano el que anotó para los visitantes, con un muy buen disparo lejano. Sesma Espinosa vio luego penalti de Marín por agarrón a Nsongo, con roja para el realista, y Yeremay puso el 3-2. El propio 10 coruñés buscó el empate, pero se encontró a Remiro, como Adama más tarde. Oyarzabal tuvo el 4-2, pero Leo Román metió una mano salvadora. Remiro rechazó un remate a bocajarro de Riki, apareciendo Oyarzabal para forzar la roja de Amatucci y 10 contra 10 la Real sujetó ya en la prolongación tres puntos que la ponen sexta.

articles.title: Alabama Fans Throw Objects at Georgia Players on Video After Loss
articles.summary: Some Alabama fans showed their displeasure toward Georgia following the Crimson Tide's 20-17 loss on Saturday night.
articles.body:
Some Alabama fans showed their displeasure toward Georgia following the Crimson Tide's 20-17 loss on Saturday night.

ESPN shared a video of the Bulldogs walking toward the tunnel and being hit with debris. Bottles and cans littered the end zone at Bryant-Denny Stadium.

Georgia survived, with Peyton Woodring's 23-yard field goal providing the difference in the outcome.

The team was perhaps fortunate to at least avoid overtime. The referees appeared to miss a pass interference penalty on the Bulldogs late in the fourth quarter. An automatic first down would've set Alabama up within field-goal range and with plenty of time to get a go-ahead touchdown.

That might've been on the minds of some inside the stadium as they deposited their concessions on the field.

The SEC has cracked down on schools for similar infractions in the past. Ole Miss was fined $75,000 in 2023 when its fans threw objects onto the field after a win over LSU. The same thing happened at Texas the following season, and the fine had climbed to $250,000.

Based on past precedent, Alabama can expect to write a six-figure check to the conference.

articles.title: Man City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 in first game after guilty verdict
articles.summary: Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki score second half goals after Ryan Gravenberch sent off.
articles.body:
Manchester City shrugged off the threat of swingeing sanctions to beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 in their first game since being found guilty on more than 100 charges of breaking Premier League financial rules.

Second half goals from Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki on Sunday extended City’s flawless start under Enzo Maresca after Ryan Gravenberch had been sent -off for two yellow cards.

Victory reestablishes City’s three-point lead at the top of the table, but the future of any title challenge rests on the outcome of the club’s appeal against widespread financial impropriety.

An independent commission found City and their Emirati owners arranged “sham” deals to artificially inflate revenues and reduce costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.2bn) between 2009 and 2018.

No sanction has yet been handed down, but a severe points deduction or even expulsion from the English top-flight is on the table unless City overturns the decision.

There has even been speculation that there could be retrospective action to strip City’s titles.

The multiple breaches of Premier League laws came during a period in which City won three titles and a clutch of other trophies.

City’s rivals believe, however, that the illegal spending during that period also built the foundations for a golden era under former boss Pep Guardiola, who left at the end of last season.

Liverpool were one of the clubs most affected, having finished second to City three times in the past 12 years.

“There are so many moments and memories we can’t get back,” Liverpool fan Martin Reilly, 23, told the AFP news agency. “They have to throw the book at them.”

City arrived under the protection of a police escort with a hostile Anfield welcome expected, but there was no repeat of the violent scenes when their team bus was pelted with bottles ahead of a Champions League clash in 2018.

Liverpool fans lined the streets to greet the visitors with chants of “cheats” and “going down”, while merchandise stalls were littered with flags and scarves mocking City’s financial scandal.

In the iconic Kop end behind one goal, a banner read “a generation of supporters cheated”.

The battles between Guardiola’s City and Jurgen Klopp’s Liverpool in recent years became the Premier League’s marquee event.

But with the eyes of the world watching today, Liverpool failed to rise to the occasion on the field.

New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola’s options were blunted without the injured Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo as the Spaniard suffered his first defeat since taking charge of the Reds.

The home side briefly flickered into life at the start of the second half when Lewis Koumas was denied a goal on his first Premier League start by Gianluigi Donnarumma.

The Abu Dhabi-backed takeover in 2008 transformed City from mid-table mediocrity into the dominant force of the English game.

City’s economic might was on full display to help turn the game, as Maresca could turn to Jeremy Doku off the bench early in the second half.

Within minutes the Belgian winger had been chopped down by Gravenberch, who was shown a second yellow card and Liverpool never recovered.

Doku’s deflected shot was then smashed home by Haaland to break the deadlock 25 minutes from time and open the floodgates.

Three minutes later Doku curled a sensational strike into the top corner himself.

Cherki then exchanged a slick one-two with Josko Gvardiol before slotting under Alisson Becker to rub salt in Liverpool’s wounds.

City midfielder Elliot Anderson told reporters after the game that his side had shown “courage” as they got the win in a hostile atmosphere.

“We have shown togetherness and fight, this is tough place to come and we have shown courage,” he said.

“It [the noise from the Anfield crowd] was more than normal … Arriving and the first 10 minutes of the first half, but we quietened the crowd and improved in the second half.

“During the game you can feel it, and it is a game where you have to stick together and we did.”

images.caption: Rayan Cherki gets past Liverpool's Jeremie Frimpong before scoring City's third at Anfield on Sunday [Michael Regan/Getty Images]
