articles.title: Liverpool 0-3 Man City: Premier League leaders make defiant statement with Anfield victory in first match since guilty verdict
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Manchester City beat 10-man Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield; Merseyside trip was City's first game since guilty verdict on all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules; Ryan Gravenberch's red card proved to be the turning point
articles.body:
The trip to Merseyside was City's first game after an independent commission found them guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules. The club have since appealed the verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

The game's turning point occurred after an hour when Ryan Gravenberch was shown a second yellow card for a foul on Jeremy Doku - a decision called "very soft" on commentary by Gary Neville. Until then, City's xG was just 0.16. From then on, the floodgates opened.

Two minutes and 36 seconds after the sending off, Erling Haaland emphatically put City ahead before Doku and Rayan Cherki turned on the style as the Premier League leaders sent a message about what they are still capable of on the pitch.

The City players were welcomed by a chorus of boos for both their warm-up and ahead of kick-off as they settled into the Anfield cauldron.

The game had mirrored the atmosphere in the early stages - frantic. The visitors were run ragged and on the receiving end of some strong tackles as the game threatened to boil over in the opening exchanges.

By half-time, City had managed to settle themselves and the crowd down. However, with Liverpool attacking The Kop in the second half, Enzo Maresca's men had to weather the storm all over again.

Gianluigi Donnarumma was on his toes to keep out multiple vicious strikes before Gravenberch's departure changed the game.

City's subsequent ruthlessness means they remain the only team to make a perfect start to the league campaign, with Andoni Iraola's Reds already nine points adrift following their first defeat.

Maresca: We need to make our own noise by winning

Man City manager Enzo Maresca speaking to Sky Sports:

"We need to learn how to deal with the noise because it will be with us in all the away games. We need to deal with that and make our noise.

"Our noise is to win games like today. At the end of the game, it was just our fans and our noise."

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland speaking to Sky Sports:

"This is part of Man City [sticking together]. For every single fan this is a lovely moment which will stay with us for a long time.

"It was tough and it was hard but, again, we show amazing character from Donnarumma all the way back to the front. I'm so proud of everyone."

"Not really [more volatile]. It was always tough to come here in the Pep and Klopp era. It's time to stay strong mentally and stick together and do what you can do something about. What we can do something about is play good football and fight together. In the end, that's the only thing we can do."

'Pep who? - Keane impressed by Man City 'statement'

"There have been lots of statements made over the last few weeks but the team made a statement today.

"The sending off was a big help but you still have to show your quality. The three goals were fantastic.

"It will be a big boost to City. They have had a good start to the season, great for [Enzo Maresca].

"You're thinking, 'Pep who?' at this stage. It's not even been mentioned the concerns we had when Pep left, or Rodri.

"Doku made a big difference going at people. He basically changed the game [off the bench] on top of the sending off."

articles.title: Liverpool 0-3 Man City: Anfield delivers own verdict on Premier League ruling but City are defiant and top of the table
articles.summary: Manchester City maintained their 100 per cent record at the top of the Premier League table with a 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield; Adam Bate reports on a surreal occasion as the Liverpool crowd let the world know how they felt about the rule-breaking City continue to deny
articles.body:
As it is, City remain top of the table having won six games from six. But this victory will not quieten the noise. They departed to boos and the accusations of cheating that were a feature of the day.

Liverpool, three times runners-up to Manchester City in 2014, 2019 and 2022, made for perfect but hostile hosts, with the Anfield crowd perhaps the ideal outlet for the emotions, a proxy for supporters everywhere. It was an atmosphere like no other.

The enterprising flag and scarf sellers in Liverpool were certainly prepared, with an unusual emphasis on the visitors, this being City's first game since an independent commission judged that they broke Premier League rules between 2009 and 2018.

City are appealing that verdict and continue to deny any wrongdoing.

But the court of opinion is making its voice heard too. Anfield has made up its mind. The banners referred to "a generation of supporters cheated" and a playful take on Wonderwall with the amended line that "you really robbed us all".

Even the choice of songs over the public-address system appeared to be pointed. Before kick-off at Anfield, we had Blame by Calvin Harris and a blast of The Joker and the Thief by Wolfmother. Upon the final whistle, it was Little Lies by Fleetwood Mac.

As expected, City's supporters opted for defiance in the face of the criticism. The boos for the Premier League anthem are nothing new but carried extra resonance. The banner declaring that 'In Khaldoon we trust' an eye-opening indication of the devotion of some.

Others preferred to shift the focus from their current predicament. There was more than a hint of nostalgia in a nod to the fact that there is far more to their club than how their rivals perceive them. Poznan dances and inflatable bananas served as a symbol of that.

The latter custom, one that dates back to Imre Varadi - 'Imre Banana' to the fans in the late '80s - is a reminder that City were always really here. This remains a proud club. The message being sent is that the downs are part of their story just as much as the ups.

But the overriding emotions inside the stadium belonged to the majority, those wearing Liverpool red, and the reality is that City and these charges are part of their story too. Anyone allowing the mind to wander at Anfield on Sunday could not escape that history.

Glance down to the spot on the turf where Steven Gerrard slipped to let in Demba Ba in 2014. Liverpool lost that game to Chelsea but lost that title to City. How can this ruling not change the tone and temperature of that regret? Sadness is now tinged with anger.

And so, for Liverpool, this is not only about City's trophies not being 'real' but those phantom triumphs of their own. "Until you've repaid the dreams you bought for your lies you'll be castaway alone under stormy skies." A banner in the Sir Kenny Dalglish Stand.

This game itself was a reminder that these matters are ongoing. The charges are historic but the consequences are part of the present.

A strange afternoon had a strange ending too - The Kop chanted 'going down' while the league table shows that City are top.

"That is the backdrop to not knowing where these points and this season is going," rued Gary Neville on commentary. "There is going to be a 'but' all the way."

articles.title: Leeds Captain Can Reach New Level, Says Ex-Star: Can Farke Unlock His Midfielder?
articles.summary: Leeds United have plenty to celebrate after returning to the Premier League and establishing themselves among the division’s competitive sides. Daniel Farke...
articles.body:
Leeds United have plenty to celebrate after returning to the Premier League and establishing themselves among the division's competitive sides. Daniel Farke needed tactical adjustments, while several important players had to prove their quality against stronger opposition. The club invested more than £100 million in new signings, including Dominic Calvert-Lewin, Anton Stach, Noah Okafor and Jaka Bijol.

Leeds United have found another level through Ampadu

Those arrivals strengthened key positions, but the contribution of established players proved just as important. Ethan Ampadu became a central figure in Leeds' midfield, combining defensive discipline with leadership and energy. His regular appearances helped Farke maintain consistency during a demanding campaign.

Former Wales international Rob Earnshaw has now praised Ampadu's development, suggesting the midfielder has more to offer. Speaking during BBC coverage of Wales against Denmark, Earnshaw highlighted his influence on Leeds' pressing, intensity and ability to recover possession.

He added that Ampadu was becoming an experienced figure for Wales, someone his teammates could trust in difficult moments. Earnshaw then compared his potential with Harry Wilson's progress, arguing that Ampadu could reach a similarly impressive standard in the Premier League.

"I think he's had one outstanding year," Earnshaw said during BBCs coverage of Wales vs Denmark.

"If you look at Leeds in the last year, their improvements and everything good that comes from Leeds and their energy and pressing and winning the ball back. He's involved with that.

"With Wales, he's now becoming the experienced one, the one you can rely on."

"I actually think there are more levels to Ethan Ampadu. I think he can really go to a new level.

"We saw Harry Wilson last year. What an outstanding year, and everybody saw he's one of the best players in the Premier League. I think Ethan Ampadu can get to those levels; there's more to come."

Can Leeds United captain Ethan Ampadu reach another level under Farke?

LONDON, ENGLAND – SEPTEMBER 09: Ethan Ampadu of Leeds United arrives at the stadium before the Carabao Cup Third Round match between Chelsea and Leeds United at Stamford Bridge on September 09, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Andrew Redington/Getty Images)

Farke's tactical decisions will play a major role in determining how far Ampadu progresses. A back-three system can give Leeds greater defensive security, while wing-backs provide width and allow midfielders to concentrate on winning possession and controlling transitions.

Calvert-Lewin offers a different dimension in attack through his aerial ability, physical presence and pressing. His movement can create space for supporting forwards, while Stach and Ampadu can help Leeds recover second balls and launch attacks quickly. However, the system requires disciplined positioning, particularly when opponents bypass the initial press.

Ampadu's value extends beyond tackles and interceptions. His reading of danger, distribution under pressure and communication help Leeds maintain their shape. Playing alongside a mobile midfielder such as Ao Tanaka could allow him to protect the defence without carrying every midfield responsibility himself.

Leeds should build their next phase around Ampadu rather than entertain speculative transfer valuations. Earnshaw's assessment makes sense because the captain already understands Farke's demands and has demonstrated that he can handle Premier League football. However, reaching the division's highest midfield bracket will require greater consistency in possession, sharper forward passing and continued defensive reliability against elite opposition.

Calvert-Lewin can improve the attack, but Ampadu gives the team its balance. If Leeds maintain that balance while improving their chance creation, their ambitions can grow without placing unrealistic expectations on one player.

articles.title: ‘Our noise is to win games’; Enzo Maresca challenges Man City to continue winning mentality
articles.summary: The Man City boss tasked his team with continuing their winning streak in order to silence opposition fans
articles.body:
Enzo Maresca declared that Manchester City brought their own noise to Anfield afte r they won 3-0 in front of a hostile Liverpool crowd in their first game since being found guilty of 114 Premier League charges.

And the City manager has challenged his team to carry on silencing opposition crowds by winning.

The Liverpool supporters called City cheats in a series of chants but Erling Haaland , Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored as Maresca's team maintained their 100 percent start to the Premier League season.

City still face potential punishments including expulsion from the top flight or a points penalty that could result in relegation.

But Maresca's team shrugged that off to record their joint biggest Premier League win at Anfield.

And the Italian said: "It was not easy for the players after the last two or three weeks but they dealt with the situation very well. I said during the week we need to learn how to deal with the outside noise because of the situation. The noise will always be there so we need to learn how to deal with that but at the same time we need to try and bring our noise, which is win games which is what we have done today.

"At the end of the game, our fans were singing so the noise was from us and not the environment. All the away games are going to be with noise so we need to learn how to deal with the noise. And at the same time, we need to make our noise. Our noise is we're singing at the end, our fans, and this has to be our target at the moment."

articles.title: Liverpool 0-3 Man City: Ryan Gravenberch's sending off in Premier League defeat criticised by Jamie Carragher
articles.summary: Man City eased to a 3-0 win at 10-man Liverpool after Ryan Gravenberch was sent off for a second bookable offence – but it was his first yellow that frustrated Jamie Carragher, who said referee Chris Kavanagh only cautioned the midfielder when he thought Elliot Anderson was hurt
articles.body:
Gravenberch, the standout player for an hour, was shown red after receiving a second yellow for a challenge on Jeremy Doku with the game tied at 0-0 in a flashpoint that turned the game, which had been finely poised, in City's favour.

Erling Haaland's opener came just two minutes and 37 seconds after Gravenberch was dismissed, and within six minutes Doku had doubled City's advantage before Rayan Cherki added a third with 12 minutes to play.

Gravenberch had picked up his first caution shortly after the restart for a foul on City midfielder Elliot Anderson, which Sky Sports pundit Carragher described as a "nothing challenge".

"It's such a poor decision by the referee," Carragher said after the game. "The thing that frustrates me is that he wasn't going to give a yellow card. He only gives it when he thinks Anderson is hurt.

"That has nothing to do with whether a foul should or should not be a yellow card."

He added: "It's barely a foul. It's a shocking decision."

"It feels really harsh when you think of the two challenges," Carragher said of Gravenberch's sending off on co-commentary.

"The first one was not a yellow card. It was so harsh for a nothing challenge on Anderson, and the referee was far too quick to get the yellow card out."

Sky Sports' Gary Neville, also on co-commentary, said Gravenberch's second yellow was "very soft", before adding: "The only thing I would say is, knowing you're on a yellow and wrong side of Doku, does he need to make the challenge?

'Liverpool looked like they had four sent off'

Manchester City had an xG of 0.16 before Gravenberch's sending off but dominated once Liverpool were down to 10 men.

Sky Sports pundit Roy Keane felt Gravenberch's dissmissal turned the match in City's favour but criticised Liverpool's response to the red card.

"I don't see how he can get a yellow card for that," Keane said of Gravenberch's first booking. "The whole game then changes.

"Liverpool struggled with the physicality. There were spaces everywhere. Liverpool looked like they had four men sent off. City were controlling it. For the first hour it was a tight game."

Daniel Sturridge was in full agreement and said the decision to award Gravenberch's first yellow card was "a joke".

"The game changed on the red card. We have to be truthful about that," Sturridge said on Sky Sports . "City delivered after the red card changed the game. Prior to that, it was very even."

Sky Sports' Micah Richards was equally puzzled about the first booking the Liverpool midfielder received. "That is soft. How is that a yellow card? I don't understand," said Richards.
